name: Peroxisomal protein import, fission and pexophagy
rationale: All members concern peroxisome biogenesis (matrix and membrane protein import, fission) or its autophagic turnover, which separates it from the peroxisomal fatty-acid oxidation and synthesis neighbours; it lacks the TYSND1 processing and unfolding terms of its superset.

qualifier: matrix protein processing (TYSND1 cleavage, unfolding, docking)
name: Peroxisomal protein import, matrix protein processing and pexophagy
rationale: Members cover peroxisomal import, fission and pexophagy plus TYSND1 cleavage, protein unfolding and membrane docking, the processing steps its smaller import/pexophagy neighbour lacks, and it has none of the fatty-acid oxidation terms of other neighbours.

name: Phenylalanine-tyrosine metabolism and phenylketonuria
rationale: All members are phenylalanine or tyrosine metabolism/catabolism terms, and the phenylketonuria and phenylalanine metabolism members distinguish it from the tyrosine-catabolism-only neighbour, while it lacks the generic amino acid catabolism terms of its superset.

name: Tyrosine catabolism downstream of phenylalanine
rationale: The three members are tyrosine catabolism and phenylalanine metabolism terms describing the single Phe-to-Tyr degradation route; it lacks the phenylketonuria and general amino acid terms of its neighbours.

name: Phenylalanine and tyrosine catabolism within broader amino acid catabolism
rationale: Members combine phenylalanine/tyrosine metabolism and phenylketonuria with generic L-amino acid, alpha-amino acid and amide catabolism terms, the generic layer its Phe/Tyr-only neighbours lack, and it has no histidine, threonine or organic acid terms.

core: Positive regulation of NK and T cell cytotoxicity
name: Enhanced NK and T cell cytotoxicity, including antitumour NK response
rationale: All three members are positive regulation of NK- or T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity, one specifically against tumour cells; unlike its superset it has no NK/T expression signatures or cytokine production, and unlike other neighbours no negative regulation or degranulation.

name: NK and T cell signatures with positive regulation of cytotoxicity
rationale: Members pair NK- and T-cell-enriched expression signatures and T cell activation with positive regulation of NK/T cytotoxicity and NK cytokine production; the signatures distinguish it from the pure-regulation neighbour and it lacks the KIR, MHC class Ib, granzyme and negative-regulation terms of others.

qualifier: excitatory and inhibitory, with postsynaptic potential regulation
name: Excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic assembly and potential regulation
rationale: Members cover PSD-95/NMDA and gephyrin/GABA receptor clustering, inhibitory synapse assembly, neurexin-neuroligin and regulation of excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic potentials; the inhibitory side distinguishes it from adhesion-focused neighbours, and it lacks the glutamatergic transmission terms of its superset.

name: Excitatory and inhibitory synapse assembly and glutamatergic transmission
rationale: Members include excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic receptor clustering and potential regulation plus neuron-neuron and positively regulated glutamatergic synaptic transmission, which the otherwise identical neighbour lacks; adhesion-focused neighbours lack the inhibitory terms.

name: Proline and glycine turnover within L-amino acid metabolism
rationale: Members are proline synthesis/catabolism, glycine synthesis, glyoxylate and glutamine-family terms with generic L-/alpha-amino acid metabolism; it lacks the organic acid umbrella terms of its superset and the aromatic, histidine or threonine terms of other neighbours.

name: Proline, glycine and glyoxylate within organic acid metabolism
rationale: Members combine proline, glycine, glyoxylate and glutamine-family amino acid terms with organic acid biosynthesis, catabolism and metabolism, the organic acid layer its nearest neighbour lacks; it has no glycine conjugation or threonine terms.

core: Pyrimidine de novo, salvage and catabolic routes
name: Pyrimidine de novo, salvage and catabolic routes with deoxyribonucleotide synthesis
rationale: Members span de novo pyrimidine synthesis, salvage and catabolism plus dTTP and deoxyribonucleotide biosynthesis; it lacks the purine deoxyribonucleoside metabolism, deoxyribonucleotide catabolism and NDP/NTP interconversion of its superset and the purine de novo terms of another neighbour.

core: Pyrimidine turnover and purine deoxyribonucleotide metabolism
name: Pyrimidine turnover and purine deoxyribonucleotide metabolism with NDP-NTP interconversion
rationale: Members cover pyrimidine synthesis, salvage and catabolism together with purine deoxyribonucleoside/dNTP metabolism, deoxyribonucleotide catabolism and nucleotide di-/triphosphate interconversion, the latter three absent from its pyrimidine-focused neighbour.

core: Viral receptor attachment, entry and cell-cell fusion
name: Coronavirus receptor attachment, endocytic entry and cell-cell fusion
rationale: Members are receptor-mediated virion attachment and endocytosis plus the coronavirus Attachment and Entry and spike-induced cell-cell fusion pathways; it lacks the dengue and RSV entry members of its superset and the influenza entry and regulatory terms of others.

name: Coronavirus, dengue and RSV attachment, entry and fusion
rationale: Members add dengue virus attachment, entry and virion assembly/release and RSV attachment and entry to the coronavirus receptor attachment, endocytosis and cell-cell fusion core, distinguishing it from the coronavirus-only neighbour; it lacks influenza entry and regulation-of-entry terms.

core: Homologous recombination repair by strand invasion
name: Homologous recombination and interstrand crosslink repair by strand invasion
rationale: Members cover strand invasion, synthesis-dependent strand annealing, sister chromatid exchange, repair synthesis and crosslink repair; it lacks the break-induced replication, unwinding and polymerase stimulation of its superset and the NHEJ, BRCA and Fanconi signalling terms of others.

qualifier: including break-induced replication and polymerase stimulation
name: Recombinational repair including break-induced replication and polymerase stimulation
rationale: Members combine strand invasion, SDSA, sister chromatid exchange and crosslink repair with break-induced replication, DNA unwinding and positive regulation of DNA polymerase activity, the latter three absent from its nearest neighbour; it has no NHEJ or checkpoint terms.

name: Control of leukocyte-endothelial adhesion and adhesion molecule production
rationale: All four members regulate leukocyte adhesion to vascular/arterial endothelium, cell adhesion molecule production or extravasation; it lacks the diapedesis and neutrophil/T cell extravasation of its superset and the monocyte, inflammatory and endothelial remodelling terms of others.

qualifier: neutrophil and T cell, with endothelial adhesion control
name: Neutrophil and T cell extravasation and endothelial adhesion control
rationale: Members add diapedesis, neutrophil and T cell extravasation and neutrophil migration to regulation of leukocyte-endothelial adhesion and adhesion molecule production; its adhesion-only neighbour lacks the extravasation terms and others are monocyte or integrin focused.

name: DHA-, EPA- and DPA-derived resolvin, protectin and maresin biosynthesis
rationale: All members synthesise D- and E-series (including aspirin-triggered) resolvins, protectins, DPA-derived maresins or DPAn-6 mediators; it lacks the tissue-regeneration conjugates, oxo-derivatives and HETE synthesis of its superset and the lipoxin/leukotriene terms of others.

name: Pro-resolving mediators, their tissue-regeneration conjugates and eicosatetraenoic acids
rationale: Members add maresin/protectin/resolvin conjugates in tissue regeneration, 13-series resolvins, electrophilic omega-3 oxo-derivatives and 5-/15-HETE synthesis to the resolvin, protectin and maresin core, distinguishing it from its subset neighbour; it lacks lipoxin and leukotriene terms.

qualifier: with 5S transcription and epigenetic rDNA control
name: RNA polymerase I and 5S rRNA transcription with epigenetic rDNA control
rationale: Members cover Pol I initiation through termination, Pol III 5S rRNA transcription and B-WICH, CSB/G9a, SIRT1 and NoRC regulation of rDNA chromatin; it lacks the MYC targets and early pre-rRNA processing of its superset and the tRNA/snRNA and translation terms of others.

name: MYC-driven rRNA transcription and early pre-rRNA processing
rationale: Members add MYC target signatures, 5'-ETS and ITS1 cleavage, rRNA 5'-end processing, facultative heterochromatin and nucleolar localisation to the Pol I/5S rRNA transcription and rDNA chromatin core, which its nearest neighbour lacks; it has no Pol III tRNA or translation terms.

name: RUNX1-controlled megakaryocyte-platelet commitment of myeloid progenitors
rationale: Members combine myeloid progenitor proliferation/differentiation and promyelocyte signatures with RUNX1-regulated megakaryocyte development, platelet morphogenesis and repression of granulocyte and erythrocyte fates; it lacks the granulopoiesis and monocyte/macrophage terms of its superset and the erythroid and HSC terms of others.

name: RUNX1-directed megakaryocyte, granulocyte and monocyte-macrophage lineage decisions
rationale: Members add transcriptional regulation of granulopoiesis and negative regulation of monocyte and macrophage differentiation to the RUNX1 megakaryocyte and myeloid progenitor core, distinguishing it from its subset neighbour; it lacks the erythroid maturation and HSC maintenance terms of others.
